Se trata del Create Chefbot Compact Connect, un robot de cocina con 24 programas automáticos, 1.200 W y una capacidad de 3,5 litros. En el Black Friday anticipado de Amazon lo tienes disponible por 127,95 euros . CREATE/CHEFBOT COMPACT CONNECT/Robot de cocina inteligente multifunción Hoy en Amazon — 127,95 € El precio podría variar. Obtenemos comisión por estos enlaces Tamaño reducido pero sin renunciar a potencia A diferencia del Monsieur Cuisine Smart de gran formato, esta versión Compact apuesta por optimizar el espacio sobre la encimera manteniendo intactas las funciones clave que hacen tan prácticos a estos ayudantes de cocina. Con una potencia máxima de 1.100 W y un rango de temperatura regulable entre 37 y 130 grados, este robot de cocina permite desde sofreír y cocer a fuego lento hasta triturar o cocinar al vapor de forma sencilla, siendo ideal incluso para los que no saben nada de cocina. En Xataka Smart Home Lidl rebaja un 54%, en su Black Friday, esta tele MiniLED de 55 pulgadas con Google TV y Dolby Atmos Uno de sus detalles que llama la atención es la forma en la que resuelve la cocina guiada sin encarecer el dispositivo con una enorme pantalla integrada. Concretamente, incorpora una pantalla táctil LCD sencilla e intuitiva en el propio cuerpo, pero se conecta con el teléfono móvil para enviar directamente más de 400 recetas desde la app oficial al robot. Su jarra de acero inoxidable ofrece una capacidad de 2,5 litros , capacidad más que suficiente para preparar raciones diarias para parejas o familias pequeñas sin ocupar el volumen de un robot gigante. Además, incorpora una báscula integrada de precisión que pesa los ingredientes directamente dentro del vaso. En cuanto a funcionamiento, ofrece 10 velocidades, giro a la derecha (para picar y triturar) y giro a la izquierda (para remover alimentos delicados sin deshacerlos). ⚡ EN RESUMEN: oferta para robot de cocina monsieur cuisine compact ✅ LO MEJOR Precio de derribo (149,99 euros): ahorrar 50 euros en un robot multifunción con báscula integrada y cocina guiada lo sitúa en una relación calidad-precio difícil de igualar. Más de 400 recetas guiadas vía smartphone: aprovecha la pantalla del móvil para seguir los pasos y enviar los ajustes directamente al robot. ❌ LO PEOR Dependencia del móvil para las recetas... Aunque tiene pantalla táctil LCD para controlar tiempo, temperatura y velocidad manualmente, es imprescindible descargar la app en el smartphone para disfrutar de la cocina guiada. Capacidad más contenida (2,5 litros)... Si sueles cocinar por lotes grandes para familias numerosas o invitados, puede quedarse algo justo frente a las jarras de 3 o 4,5 litros de los modelos mayores. 💡 CÓMPRALO SI... Tienes una cocina pequeña o con poca encimera libre, vives solo, en pareja o en una familia de tres miembros, y quieres iniciarte en los robots de cocina con un modelo completo, fiable y por menos de 150 euros. ⛔ NO LO COMPRES SI... Buscas un robot con una gran pantalla integrada en el propio aparato para no depender del teléfono móvil mientras cocinas, o si necesitas preparar grandes cantidades de domida de una sola vez. noticias.titulo: APOD: 2026 November 19 – The Horsehead and Flame Nebulas
noticias.resumen: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 19 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. OriginalAnnotated The […]
noticias.contenido: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 19 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Original Annotated The Horsehead and Flame Nebulas Explanation: Today’s image could have been a painting. But what do these colors mean? The brightest star, left of the center, is blue Alnitak (the Girdle): a triple star system best known for being the easternmost star in Orion’s Belt . The instantly recognizable shape of a dark horse’s head at the center is the aptly named Horsehead Nebula . It is about five light-years tall and lies approximately 1,500 light-years away. It is made of dust and gas that obscure the red glow behind it, which is caused by hydrogen gas being ionized by the bright star Sigma Orionis at the top. The orange nebula with dark filaments on the left is the Flame Nebula . Closer to the Horsehead, the blue reflection nebula NGC 2023 is actively forming stars. The data for this “painting” were collected for almost six hours at the Utah Desert Remote Observatories , but the equipment was remotely controlled by the astrophotographer from his home, over 2,000 km away in Illinois . Tomorrow’s picture: what’s next? Date November 19, 2026 Credit Mark E. noticias.titulo: El Niño Rains Paint the Atacama
noticias.resumen: Winter precipitation helped wake dormant seeds in northern Chile, carpeting the desert with what may be the region’s most extensive flowering of the satellite era.
noticias.contenido: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory El Niño Rains Paint the Atacama Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search September 14 October 24 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 14 October 24 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 14 October 24 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Parts of the Atacama Desert in northern Chile, normally one of the driest places on Earth, turned red-purple, green, and white in austral spring 2026 following an unusually wet winter. The rain woke seeds lying dormant in the soil, setting off what scientists say may be the most extensive desierto florido , or “flowering desert,” of the satellite era. The rains came as El Niño was strengthening in the tropical Pacific. During an El Niño, the subtropical Pacific high that normally keeps the region dry weakens, while a blocking high tends to form in the South Pacific near the tip of South America. Together, these shifts push the Southern Hemisphere storm track equatorward. Beginning in mid-July, a series of storm fronts fed by an atmospheric river brought one of the heaviest July rain events in decades to a long stretch of Chile, from the Atacama region south to Los Lagos, according to Chile’s national weather service (Dirección Meteorológica de Chile). In August, back-to-back winter storms blanketed parts of the Atacama Desert in rare snow . The spring blooms that followed are visible in these satellite image pairs, which show the desert at different stages of flowering on September 14 (left) and on October 24 (right). The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 acquired the September images, and the OLI on Landsat 9 acquired the October images. The pair above shows a part of the desert about 30 kilometers (20 miles) southwest of Copiapó, near the eastern sector of Desierto Florido National Park. The red-purple areas prominent in the October 24 scene are vast blooms of pata de guanaco, most likely Cistanthe longiscapa or another Cistanthe species, according to Roberto Chávez, a remote sensing scientist at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso. Patches of red-purple Cistanthe are visible during a bloom in the Atacama Desert, shown in this photograph taken on October 24, 2026. Matías Pérez-Evens and Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso. Chávez and colleagues photographed the Cistanthe blooms (above) in the area that same day. They were in the field to study the bloom with satellite data, drones, and digital cameras. The project aims to use these data to map how the bloom’s biodiversity changes across space and over time, to inform land-use planners and conservation managers. The pair below shows another part of the blooming desert, about 50 kilometers (30 miles) southwest of Copiapó. It lies within a priority area of the desert cited for its biological significance, including the flowering landscape. september 14 october 24 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison september 14 october 24 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison september 14 october 24 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Cistanthe is abundant here in the October view, but the September scene (left) reveals another desert beauty. The green areas capped with white are blooms of suspiros, or Nolana , probably Nolana baccata , according to Andres Moreira-Muñoz, a scientist at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso who studies plant geography. The researchers photographed the Nolana -covered hillsides below on September 24, 2026. White Nolana blankets a hillside in the Atacama Desert during a bloom, shown in this photograph taken on September 24, 2026. Matías Pérez-Evens and Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso. Satellite data have been key to understanding the Atacama’s blooms. A 2014 study used Landsat observations to map where flowering and fog-fed plants grow around the Copiapó dune field. And a 2019 study used NASA’s long-term vegetation record to identify 13 Atacama Desert blooms between 1981 and 2015. Compared with those past blooms, the 2026 event stands out. “This instance of the ‘blooming desert’ phenomenon appears to be the most significant to date—in terms of its extent, intensity, and duration,” Moreira-Muñoz said, “at least since we began using remote sensing.” NASA Earth Observatory images by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey . Photos by Matías Pérez-Evens and Roberto O. Chávez/LabGRS-Instituto de Geografía- Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso, Chile, acquired during Fondecyt Regular Project 1251184 (ANID, Chile): Spatiotemporal variation of Flowering Desert biodiversity via multispectral remote sensing. Story by Kathryn Hansen. noticias.contenido: A mountain range can bear the marks of events from tens of millions of years ago. The challenge lies in determining when each mark was created. noticias.titulo: New mixing benchmark could help industry reduce energy use in stirred tanks
noticias.resumen: Solid–liquid mixing, where particles are dispersed in a liquid, is essential in many industrial processes such as slurry preparation, crystallization, precipitation, adsorption and dissolution. In such cases, effective mixing is critical for contact between particles and liquid, enabling mass transfer. Floating particles often pose a challenge in mixing because they are lighter than the liquid and tend to float at its surface. While impeller agitation does draw them into the liquid, the minimum mixing intensity needed for effective drawdown has been difficult to define.

noticias.contenido: Country: Yemen Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. IOM Yemen DTM continues to record displacement caused by the escalation in western Yemen. As of 17 November 2026, IOM Yemen DTM recorded an increase of 9,281 individual IDPs compared to the figure presented in the RDT report distributed on 16 November 2026, bringing displacement between 1 August and 17 November to approximately 356,602 individuals (59,426 households)1. This brings the cumulative number recorded since the escalation began in June 2026 to 357,658 individuals (59,602 households). The largest concentration of displaced people was reported in Ta’iz Governorate, hosting 145,344 individuals (41%), followed by Lahj Governorate with 95,580 individuals (27%), and Aden Governorate with 71,706 individuals (20%). Additional displacement was recorded in Abyan with 17,208 individuals (5%); Al Hodeidah with 8,244 individuals (2%)2; Shabwah with 6,183 individuals (2%); Ma’rib with 4,104 individuals (1%); Hadramawt with 3,576 individuals (1%); Al Maharah with 3,096 individuals (less than 1%); and Ad Dali’ with 2,617 individuals (less than 1%).

noticias.contenido: Countries: Ethiopia, Djibouti, Kenya, Somalia, Sudan, Uganda, Yemen Source: International Organization for Migration Please refer to the attached file. In Ethiopia, FM data is gathered in five of the country’s land crossborder points, namely: Dawele, Galafi, Metema, Moyale and Tog Wajale FMPs. In Kurmuk, data collection has been interrupted since 3 February 2026 due to insecurity in the border area. Between 1 and 30 June 2026, a total of 107,719 movements were identified across the assessed five FMPs in Ethiopia, highlighting continued population mobility along key migration routes. Outgoing movements (58,188 individuals) accounted for the largest share of observed flows (54.0%), whereas incoming movements (49,531 individuals) accounted for 46.0 per cent of observed flows. This indicates that more individuals exited the monitored areas compared to those that entered.

noticias.contenido: Countries: South Sudan, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Nigeria Source: World Health Organization Please refer to the attached file. PRIORITY ACTIONS Sustain BVD preparedness as the DRC outbreak reaches 11,376 cases and 5,568 deaths (CFR 48.9%); maintain PoE screening (83,826 events over 14–16 Nov) and screen air arrivals at Juba International Airport. Strengthen cross-border surveillance on the Yei–Morobo–Kaya corridor given spread to Watsa (Haut-Uélé) and cases in Aru and Ariwara; sustain alert investigation and testing in Yei, Morobo and Yambio. Sustain cholera response in Fangak and Renk (Rubkona and Mayom have had no cases since 30 October) and investigate the Aweil West (Wedweil) cluster of 67 mostly untested cases; drive 100% RDT testing toward the earliest end-of-outbreak declaration (8 December). Deliver the Round 2 polio NIDs (17–20 November; 87% readiness) and sustain measles response; the Magwi reactive campaign is completed (12,953 under-fives), with Malakal and Canal/Pigi campaigns being planned. Investigate the six suspected human anthrax cases in Jur River (Western Bahr el Ghazal) and sustain Guinea worm surveillance (no human or animal case in 2026); maintain malaria response (48,675 cases, 47% below 2025).

noticias.contenido: Country: Yemen Sources: Health Cluster, World Health Organization Please refer to the attached file. Key Highlights Casualties continue, with Marib and Lahj carrying the burden. The HEOC count reached 12,779 (10,519 injured, 2,260 deaths) by 16 November, +1,024 in eight days. The daily average fell to ~128 from ~225, but reporting was incomplete (58–92% a day, none for 9–10 November), so the figures are a minimum. Between 11 and 15 November, Marib reported 266 casualties and 49 deaths and Lahj 234 casualties; Al-Dhale’e still has no funded WHO-supported trauma deployment. The front line is moving towards Aden. Front lines moved rapidly through Lahj and are approaching Aden, which hosts the main referral hospitals, the Health Emergency Operations Centre and the warehouse supplying the response. Further movement may change casualty flows and displacement, disrupt referral and supply routes, and require WHO and partners to adapt their operations. Measles–rubella campaign reached 92.3% of target. MoPHP results show 883,896 children aged 6–59 months vaccinated and 741,713 given vitamin A (77.5%). Al-Mahrah (61%) and Socotra (78%) fell short and 73,300 children were not reached. WHO-supported teams vaccinated 6,007 displaced children in five IDP camps in Aden and Lahj. Displacement continues to be at about 3,150 households a week. IOM DTM has recorded 347,321 people displaced since 1 August, including 18,780 in the past week, of whom 55% went to Lahj and 30% went to Taiz. Cholera is falling in the five most-affected governorates, but a complex outbreak is growing in Tarim. Suspected cases fell from 638 (W40) to 321 (W45). Tarim (Hadramout Al-Wadi) has reported 172 cases of acute diarrhea since W43, 78 RDT-positive and 22 culture-confirmed, with both suspected food and water. A diarrhea treatment center is being set up. Fuel and medical supplies are critically short in Taiz. Severe shortages of fuel, surgical supplies and anesthesia medicines are disrupting emergency services, including operating theatres and oxygen generation for intensive care units, and hospitals cannot sustain the continuous pressure. WHO delivered 19.6 MT of medicines and supplies to three facilities, and IRY and FMF plan to support two city hospitals. Shortages are also reported across the front line. Health facilities in areas under the control of the de facto authorities are reported to be short of medical and surgical supplies. Alternative delivery routes and access negotiations are needed to reach hospitals on both sides. The trauma referral pathway has critical gaps. Only four of the 35 planned trauma stabilization points are funded, none of them in Aden or in the part of Lahj towards which the front line is moving, and referral dispatch is unfunded. Burn cases are rising, yet hospitals can offer little beyond initial stabilization and wound dressing. Mental health and psychosocial support and rehabilitation remain the weakest links, leaving patients without continuity of care. Funding remains the binding constraint. All 32 WHO-supported trauma deployments are funded only until January 2027. WHO’s third CERF request is being consolidated at US$2.4 million, including sites, mobile teams and supplies proposed by UNICEF and IOM.

noticias.autor: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
noticias.contenido: Country: Somalia Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Please refer to the attached file. Review Summary: Significant local rains in the south, little rain in the centre and north. During 10–16 November, Bualle recorded 159.9 mm, Balcad 115.0 mm and Awdheegle 88.4 mm, while most stations in Bay, Hiraan and the centre recorded little or no rain. In the north, Las Dacawo recorded 50.0 mm and Elafweyn 31.5 mm. Satellite estimates (IMERG, 11–17 November) indicate 30–55 mm over Lower Juba and parts of Middle Juba and Gedo. By 16 November, 37 stations, 33 of them with a Deyr normal above 15 mm, had already received their full Deyr normal, including Baidoa (405.5 mm, 176% of the Deyr normal), Galkacyo (253.5 mm, 390%), Awdheegle (265.2 mm, 169%) and Bualle (240.9 mm, 148%), which passed its normal this week. Borama (16%), Burao (21%), Luuq (25%) and Mogadishu (27%) remain far below normal. River levels are rising slightly on the upper Shabelle and the Juba but remain well below flood-risk levels. Belet Weyne rose from 2.90 m on 15 November to 3.76 m today, 2.74 m below its moderate flood-risk level. Jowhar (2.90 m) and Bulo Burti (2.30 m) are falling, and Dollow (2.86 m) and Luuq (2.78 m) are rising slowly. Flood water in Jowhar district is receding. Satellite images show about 55 km² of flood water in Jowhar district, down from about 87 km² last week. Radio Ergo callers (5–11 November) reported flash floods that drowned livestock at Garadag in Sanaag and a death in stagnant flood water in Hirshabelle, while many callers in the south and centre welcomed the rains and said they had not seen the floods mentioned in the alerts.
